_comment: Example PSMutant config. Copy into your repo, point `mutate` at pure/DB-free modules and `tests` at the Pester files that cover them. Paths are relative to -SourceRoot (default: current dir). Run: Invoke-PSMutation -ConfigFile ./psmutant.config.json
_operators: The four below are the default set. Four more are opt-in: StringLiteral (quoted string -> ''), ConditionalBoundary (-gt <-> -ge, -lt <-> -le), ConditionForcing (an if/elseif condition -> $true and -> $false) and ReturnValue (return <expr> -> return $null). ConditionForcing is the one to add if a file scores 100% while producing almost no mutants: a decision like `if ($SyncUsers) { ... }` holds no comparison, literal or negation, so nothing in the default set can perturb it and the 100% is vacuous. Adding any operator roughly doubles the mutant count and lowers the score, so expect to lower thresholds.break before raising it again - and it renumbers mutants, so existing reports can no longer seed a -RecheckFrom run.
_timeout: Each mutant runs under a wall-clock timeout = max(timeoutFloorSeconds, baseline x timeoutFactor). A non-terminating mutant (e.g. a mutated loop body) is cut off and counted as Killed instead of hanging the run. Both optional; defaults 4 and 15.
